implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX only. There are NO ordinary stack arguments, and that is derived rather than assumed: the prologue pushes exactly three words (0x00fa73c0, 0x00fa73c1, 0x00fa73ca), the epilogue pops exactly three (0x00fa7448, 0x00fa7449, 0x00fa744a), and abi_derived.parse reports frame {fp false, sub null, lea_esp null, and_esp null, mov_ebp_esp false} with local_extent 0, so the body has no frame slots that an argument could live in. Every word the body pushes for a callee is dropped either by the body itself (0x00fa7400 ADD ESP,0xc) or by that callee (ret 4), so at 0x00fa7448 ESP is back on its entry value. Ghidra's own record carries parameter_count 0 and signature "undefined FUN_00fa73c0(void)"; the decompilation models the receiver as an explicit `int param_1`, which is the same single receiver seen through a stack-slot fiction and does not imply a second argument.
implementation.helper_symbol: extern "C" Word snap_delta_step(Word range_first, Word cursor); -- the six instructions 0x00fa73d9..0x00fa73ec factored out so the model test can drive THIS code over the whole 32-bit domain instead of a handful of hand-picked inputs. The body calls it and touches nothing in between, so the factoring is not observable. Its spelling carries NO address, and that is deliberate on both counts: not 0x00fa73c0, which is the entry of the body under reconstruction and belongs to sw1_snap_and_dispatch_00fa73c0 alone, and not 0x00fa73d9 either, because unlike for_each_stride_ac_00f9f770 and select_from_table_a_00fbaf10 -- which ARE real CALL targets -- this helper is a fragment folded out of the target and not a callee, so an address in its name would read as a transfer of control the body never makes (0x00fa73d9 is `SUB EDI,EBX`, the first instruction of the body and the start of nothing). It is named for what it computes; the six addresses are in the .cpp comments. This was the repair of 2026-09-28: the helper was previously spelled snap_delta_00fa73c0, and see known_blockers for why that name was load-bearing on the wrong side.
implementation.receiver_model: a 0x818-byte opaque run. Exactly five displacements are reached -- 0x28, 0x20c, 0x798, 0x79c, 0x814 -- and exactly two words are written (0x79c and 0x814). The machine-derived receiver record is bounds_only with offsets [40, 524, 1944, 1948, 2068], distinct_offsets 5, max_offset 2068, written_through 2, register ECX, shape R-ALIAS, so it says where the body reached and not what any word is for. NO member is named anywhere. 0x818 is 0x814 + 4, the last byte the body writes, and is not a claim about the class.
implementation.dispatch_model: three indirect calls, all through the same chain and all at table dword index 6 (displacement 0x18), each re-resolved from the receiver rather than cached. Two levels of indirection: receiver+0x28 holds a pointer to a sub-object, and the DISPATCH WORD is that sub-object's own word 0. The receiver of each dispatched call is the level-0 value, because ECX still holds it at the CALL. The model declares the slot displacement as a single named constant and the model test fills table indices 0..8 with eighteen distinct markers so that an off-by-one-slot or wrong-table reconstruction calls a different identity.
implementation.dependency_note: all three direct callees are declared extern in the package header and defined as observers in the package's own model test; no other package's header is included. 0x00f9f770, 0x00fbaf10, 0x00fbaf50 and 0x00ac9480 are not owned by this package and this package asserts nothing about them beyond what their own instruction bytes fix: their terminator form, their stack-argument shape and their argument order.

observed_original_abi.receiver_alias: ESI (MOV ESI,ECX at 0x00fa73c2; every receiver access in the body goes through that alias, including the last one at 0x00fa7442, which is why the machine-derived receiver record reports register ECX with shape R-ALIAS)
observed_original_abi.return_type_note: The records disagree about this and all three positions are recorded rather than picked silently. abi.return_semantics is the string "unclassified_in_EAX"; abi_derived.return is {register EAX, register_class aggregate_unknown, type null, void_possible false}; ghidra_function.return_type is the unresolved string "undefined". The live decompilation of this VA is `void __fastcall FUN_00fa73c0(int param_1)` with an explicit bare `return;`. The machine settles it as far as it can: the last instruction that writes EAX on any path is 0x00fa741e `MOV EAX,[EDX+0x18]`, the third dispatch's target load, after which the body only CALLs twice and INCs a memory word -- and 0x00fa7442 does not touch EAX. So EAX is live at 0x00fa744b holding 0x00fbaf50's own return word, and nothing in this body writes a value there for its caller. void is what the bytes support. abi_derived's own abstained_because note is the related caveat: "flow_not_modelled: the linear ESP walk ends at +20, so the listing is not one path", which is true of the tool's walker (the three indirect calls break it) and is resolved here by the explicit ledger in mechanics.frame_ledger. Two rules are recorded here because the validator is sensitive to both. (1) "unclassified_in_EAX" is a REGISTER-CLASS classification in the derived layer's own vocabulary, not a C or C++ type: it is stated here as a machine phrase and nowhere else, and it must never be given a name -- no typedef, alias, using-declaration or enum carries it, and no declaration in sw1_00fa73c0_types.hpp is spelled after it, because a source type named after a register class would be a claim the machine does not make. abi.return_type, the only string the string-agreement arm reads, is the separate field above and is "void". (2) The 2026-09-28 RETURN SEMANTICS blocker was NOT a disagreement between void and unclassified_in_EAX: those two fields are different kinds of statement and the check only compares the former. It was the validator reading the span of the wrong definition -- see known_blockers.
observed_original_abi.callee_conventions: each fixed by the callee's own bytes, read from this image: 0x00f9f770 is 0x38 bytes, 0x00f9f770..0x00f9f7a7, and BOTH of its exits are a bare `c3` with no immediate (0x00f9f7a0 on the loop exit, 0x00f9f7a7 on the early return), so it returns without touching ESP and 0x00fa7400 `ADD ESP,0xc` is the caller's cleanup -- cdecl with three words. 0x00fbaf10 ends `c2 04 00` (RET 0x4) and 0x00fbaf50 ends `c2 04 00`, both taking their receiver in ECX (0x00fbaf10's first comparison is against [ECX+0x5c0]; 0x00fbaf55 is MOV EDI,ECX) -- both __thiscall with one stack word, callee-owned cleanup. The three dispatch targets are bound to the same convention by the ledger, not by a comment.
observed_original_abi.evidence_level: ABI_INFERRED (abi_derived.verdict ABI_INFERRED, abi_derived.conventions.confidence INFERRED, abi_derived.completeness CORE_RESOLVED, abi_derived.receiver.confidence SUPPORTED)

mechanics.body_shape: read two words out of the receiver; hand a triple to a cdecl range walk that is degenerate for this caller; snap one of those two words toward the other in whole 0xac steps; resolve a two-level dispatch chain three times and call one table slot with three immediates; call two thiscall methods on a different sub-object with the literal 0; increment a counter; return void

frame_ledger.method: one linear walk of ESP through all 46 instructions, using each callee's own terminator to settle the stack after every transfer. Entry ESP is 0.
walk: 0x00fa73c0 PUSH EBX -> -4 (saved EBX, read back by 0x00fa744a)
0x00fa73c1 PUSH ESI -> -8 (saved ESI, read back by 0x00fa7449)
0x00fa73ca PUSH EDI -> -12 (saved EDI, read back by 0x00fa7448)
0x00fa73d4 CALL 0x00f9f770 -> -28; its bare RET pops the return address -> -24
0x00fa7400 ADD ESP,0xc -> -12 (the only stack adjustment in the body)
0x00fa7403 PUSH 0x0536250c -> -16; 0x00fa7408 CALL -> -20; the callee's ret 4 pops the return address and its own word -> -12
0x00fa7448 POP EDI -> -8; 0x00fa7449 POP ESI -> -4; 0x00fa744a POP EBX -> 0
0x00fa744b RET -> +4, which is the caller's ESP as its own CALL left it
two_consequences: The frame carries no ordinary arguments. Three words go down and three come up, and every argument word is dropped by the body or by its callee. The signature is __thiscall with a receiver and nothing else.

Each of the three dispatched callees MUST remove its own pushed word. The body never executes a second ADD ESP, so a bare-RET callee would leave ESP at -16 after the first call; the three epilogue POPs would then read the three immediates instead of the saved registers and the RET would jump to the wrong address. The bare-RET variant of the same walk ends at -12 instead of 0 and therefore does NOT balance. The model test computes both walks and requires the first to balance and the second not to.
frame_ledger.corroboration: abi_derived.parse independently reports frame {fp false, sub null, lea_esp null, and_esp null, mov_ebp_esp false} and local_extent 0, and abi.cleanup reports {bytes 0, side caller} with the evidence string "ret with no immediate, no stack reads" -- which is exactly the shape this walk produces. The three saved registers in the abi record (EBX, EDI, ESI) are the three this prologue pushes.

receiver_displacement.0x28: read three times, at 0x00fa73f8, 0x00fa740a and 0x00fa7419, once per dispatch. It is a POINTER TO A SUB-OBJECT, not a dispatch word: 0x00fa73fb dereferences it (`MOV EDX,[ECX]`) and 0x00fa73fd dereferences what comes back. The model test plants a poison word at the receiver's own +0x00 and a decoy function pointer at the sub-object's own +0x18 so that a one-level reconstruction calls the decoy.
receiver_displacement.0x20c: read twice, at 0x00fa7428 and 0x00fa7435, once per 0xfbaf* call. Also a pointer -- both callees dereference their own ECX. Re-read rather than reused, which the model test proves by re-pointing it from inside the first callee.
receiver_displacement.0x798: read once, at 0x00fa73c4, into EBX. It is the third argument of the 0x00f9f770 call and the fixed point of the snap. Never written.
receiver_displacement.0x79c: read at 0x00fa73cb into EDI and read-modify-written at 0x00fa73f2. It is BOTH the first and the second argument of the 0x00f9f770 call (0x00fa73d2 and 0x00fa73d3 push the same register) and the word the snap moves.
receiver_displacement.0x814: read-modify-written once, at 0x00fa7442, the last thing the body does. A 32-bit INC of memory, so it wraps.

range_call_1.convention: cdecl (bare `c3` at both 0x00f9f7a0 and 0x00f9f7a7; the caller drops the three words at 0x00fa7400)
range_call_1.argument_order: fixed by the callee's own frame reads, not by its decompilation: 0x00f9f771 `MOV EBX,[ESP+0xc]` with ESP at entry-4 is entry+8, i.e. argument 2, and 0x00f9f776 `MOV ESI,[ESP+0xc]` with ESP at entry-8 is entry+4, i.e. argument 1. The third word is read at 0x00f9f7a1 `MOV EAX,[ESP+0x14]` with ESP at entry-8, i.e. entry+0xc, and again at 0x00f9f77f `MOV EDI,[ESP+0x18]` with ESP at entry-12, i.e. the same entry+0xc on the loop path, where it is the receiver for the per-element thiscall 0x00f9f620.
range_call_1.callee_behaviour: it compares its arguments 1 and 2 for equality first (0x00f9f77a) and, on equality, jumps to 0x00f9f7a1 and returns its third word. Otherwise it walks [argument1, argument2) in 0xac steps (0x00f9f78b `ADD ESI,0xac`, 0x00f9f791 `ADD EDI,0xac`) calling 0x00f9f620 on the parallel word and returns the advanced parallel pointer.
range_call_1.degenerate_for_this_caller: PROVEN, not inferred. 0x00fa73d2 and 0x00fa73d3 push EDI both times, so arguments 1 and 2 are bit-for-bit equal and the equality branch is always taken. The callee never enters its loop, never reaches 0x00f9f620, and returns the word the caller already had in EBX. That word is then dead: the very next instruction, 0x00fa73d9 `SUB EDI,EBX`, does not read EAX. The model still performs the call, because it is in the listing and its three arguments are observable, and the model test asserts both the argument identity and the deadness -- the whole body is run twice from identical starting bytes with two different poisoned return values and the resulting receivers must be byte-identical.
range_call_1.arguably_still_unknown: whether the words at receiver+0x798 and +0x79c are pointers at all. This body never dereferences them and 0x00f9f770 does not on the degenerate path. The model passes them through as opaque void* and the fixtures plant small non-dereferenceable integers, so a reconstruction that invented a dereference would fail the test rather than pass it quietly.

snap_arithmetic.instructions: 0x00fa73d9 SUB EDI,EBX / 0x00fa73db MOV EAX,0xd05f417d / 0x00fa73e0 IMUL EDI / 0x00fa73e2 SAR EDX,0x5 / 0x00fa73e5 MOV EAX,EDX / 0x00fa73e7 SHR EAX,0x1f / 0x00fa73ea ADD EAX,EDX / 0x00fa73ec IMUL EAX,EAX,0xac / 0x00fa73f2 ADD [ESI+0x79c],EAX
machine_details: SUB is a 32-bit subtract, so the delta WRAPS. A reconstruction that formed the difference in 64 bits and narrowed afterwards would differ for base 0x80000000 / cursor 0 and for base 1 / cursor 0; the model test drives both.
IMUL EDI is the signed one-operand form, giving a 64-bit product in EDX:EAX of which only EDX is used.

SHR EAX,0x1f is LOGICAL, so the add-sign correction contributes 1 for a negative EDX and 0 otherwise -- not -1, which is what a C++ `>> 31` on a signed value gives. This is the difference between truncating and flooring division and it is one of the model test's named refutations.
IMUL EAX,EAX,0xac is a 32-bit multiply and the store is a 32-bit add, so both wrap. The model does the multiply and the accumulate in unsigned arithmetic for exactly this reason.
0x00fa73f2 is a READ-MODIFY-WRITE of memory, so the model re-reads the word from the receiver rather than reusing the register copy.
snap_arithmetic.identity: over the whole 32-bit signed domain the amount added is exactly -(trunc(delta / 172)) * 172, with trunc() the C++ signed integer division (rounding toward zero) and delta = cursor - range_first taken modulo 2^32. Concretely: a delta that is an exact multiple of 0xac puts the word at +0x79c exactly onto the word at +0x798; anything else leaves a residue of the same sign with magnitude below 0xac; delta 0x80000000 adds 0x7ffffff8 and delta 0x7fffffff adds 0x80000008.
snap_arithmetic.identity_proof: checked over 44,291,668 deltas in the model test: exhaustively on [-2^20, 2^20]; on every multiple of 172 across the whole signed domain (the class where a floor-versus-truncate error is largest); on a stride of 251 across the whole domain, which is prime and coprime with 172 and therefore hits every residue class mod 172 many times over; and, with six different fixed points, on a strided window. The oracle is the closed form, computed independently of the model's magic-number emulation, so a mistake in one cannot hide behind a matching mistake in the other.
snap_arithmetic.coherence_note: 0xac is the same constant twice -- the IMUL immediate here and the stride 0x00f9f770 steps both of its cursor words by. That is an observation about two instruction bytes and is not turned into a claim about what 0xac is a unit of.

virtual_dispatch.chain: level 0 0x00fa73f8 `MOV ECX,[ESI+0x28]` (and again at 0x00fa740a, 0x00fa7419) -> level 1 `MOV EDX,[ECX]` at 0x00fa73fb / 0x00fa740d / 0x00fa741c -> level 2 `MOV EAX,[EDX+0x18]` at 0x00fa73fd / 0x00fa740f / 0x00fa741e -> `CALL EAX` at 0x00fa7408 / 0x00fa7417 / 0x00fa7426.
virtual_dispatch.two_levels: the word at receiver+0x28 is a pointer to an object; the DISPATCH WORD is that object's word 0. A reconstruction that read the table word straight out of receiver+0x28 would be reading an object the machine never touches.
virtual_dispatch.slot: displacement 0x18, i.e. dword index 6 counting from the dispatch word.
virtual_dispatch.reload: the chain is resolved afresh before every one of the three calls. Observable, and the model test proves both halves separately: case R4 re-points the sub-object's own dispatch word from inside the first callee and requires calls 2 and 3 to land on the new table; case R4b re-points the RECEIVER's word at +0x28 and requires calls 2 and 3 to receive the new sub-object. A mutation that cached the resolved function survives R4 alone; one that cached the level-0 pointer survives R4b alone. Both were observed surviving before the corresponding case was added.
virtual_dispatch.arguments: one stack word each, callee-cleaned, and ECX still holding the level-0 sub-object pointer at the CALL -- so the call is a thiscall on the sub-object. The three immediates are 0x0536250c, 0x0536250d and 0x03a23f9a in that order.
virtual_dispatch.constants_not_named: nothing in this repository says what the three immediates are, and this package does not guess. That the first two are adjacent integers is recorded as an observation about their bit patterns only. For the integrator: 0x0536250c and 0x0536250d each appear as a `PUSH imm32` at six places in .text (0x00f32e13/0x00f32e56, 0x00f3564f/0x00f35680, 0x00f36a81/0x00f36ab5, 0x00f9b592/0x00f9b5eb, 0x00fa7403/0x00fa7412 and 0x00faa480/0x00faa4bc) and 0x03a23f9a at four (0x00f9b4b3, 0x00f9b520, 0x00fa7421, 0x00faa3cf), so they are ordinary ID-shaped immediates rather than unique to this body, and no name is asserted.
virtual_dispatch.record_disagreement: abi_derived.dispatch records {indirect_calls 3, call_offsets [], vtable_shaped_loads 0}. The 3 agrees with the listing. The 0 for vtable_shaped_loads does not: the tool does not classify `MOV EDX,[ECX]` / `MOV EAX,[EDX+0x18]` as a vtable-shaped pair. The listing is followed here, and the disagreement is recorded rather than smoothed over.
virtual_dispatch.not_this_table: the table at 0x01490be8 is the RECEIVER's class table, NOT the dispatch table of the object at receiver+0x28, and the two must not be conflated. This body is at that table's displacement +0x70, so it is an entry of it. But its slot +0x18 holds 0x00fa0d70, whose own seven bytes are `8b 81 cc 01 00 00 / c3` -- `MOV EAX,[ECX+0x1cc]; RET`, a ZERO-argument getter with a bare RET that removes no stack word. A callee that removed nothing would leave the stack twelve bytes short at 0x00fa7448, so the object at receiver+0x28 cannot be one of that table. The neighbouring slot +0x1c of the same table does hold the required shape (0x00fa0d90 is `8b 44 24 04 / 89 81 d0 01 00 00 / c2 04 00`, a one-argument callee-cleaned setter), which is why the two tables are kept apart here. No table, class, member or slot is named in the model, and the model test plants its own tables rather than trying to reproduce 0x01490be8.

direct_call_2.convention: __thiscall (ends `c2 04 00`; receiver in ECX -- its first comparison is `CMP DWORD PTR [ECX+0x5c0],EAX`)
direct_call_2.arguments: the immediate 0, pushed by the one-byte `6a 00` at 0x00fa742e, and in ECX the word at receiver+0x20c
direct_call_2.callee_behaviour: returns immediately at 0x00fbaf41 if the receiver's word at +0x5c0 already equals the argument, if the argument is negative, or if it is at least 0x10. Otherwise it stores the argument at the receiver's +0x5c0, computes `LEA EAX,[EAX*4+0x16d6d30]`, writes that back over its own argument slot, adds 0x20c to ECX and tail-jumps to 0x00ac9480, which is itself __thiscall with one stack word and ends `c2 04 00`. With the argument 0 this caller always passes, the store and the tail call happen unless the sub-object's +0x5c0 already holds 0.
direct_call_2.not_asserted: whether the receiver's +0x5c0 already holds 0, and what 0x00ac9480 would do, are properties of the sub-object. The observer implements both branches and the model asserts neither.

direct_call_3.arguments: the immediate 0, pushed by the one-byte `6a 00` at 0x00fa743b, and in ECX the word at receiver+0x20c, RE-READ from the receiver at 0x00fa7435 rather than reused
direct_call_3.callee_behaviour: returns at 0x00fbaf99 if the receiver's word at +0x5c4 already equals the argument. Otherwise it stores the argument at +0x5c4, fetches the outgoing pointer from the receiver's +0x1f4 and the incoming one from `MOV ESI,[EAX*4+0x16d6d70]`, calls through the incoming pointer's table slot 0, stores it at +0x1f4, and calls through the outgoing pointer's table slot 1.
direct_call_3.two_different_operations: 0x00fbaf10 stores its identifier at the receiver's +0x5c0 and biases ECX by +0x20c before a tail call; 0x00fbaf50 stores at +0x5c4 and walks the receiver's +0x1f4. That difference is in the two callees' bytes and is why the model keeps two calls rather than folding them into one. The model test checks it: the two observers write to +0x5c0 and +0x5c4 respectively, so folding the pair would lose one of the two stores.
direct_call_3.not_recoverable_here: the tables at 0x016d6d30 and 0x016d6d70 that these two callees index lie outside every section header in this file (.data has VMA 0x0150c000 and size 0x000c4c00, so it ends at 0x015d0c00; .tls begins at 0x0171f000). Their contents are therefore NOT recoverable from this image, and nothing is claimed about the words the callees would fetch. The observers fabricate them freely and the model asserts nothing about that boundary.

mechanics.control_flow: ZERO conditional branches. All 46 instructions are straight-line: there is no Jcc, no CALL rel32 loop, no jump table and no intra-procedural JMP anywhere in the body. Every conditional decision the body makes is made inside a callee, and the model test drives the callees' outcomes rather than the body's branches. This is the reason the model has no `if` at all.
mechanics.globals: none. No instruction in the 46 names a data-segment address. Every absolute operand in the body is either a code address (the three CALL rel32s) or an immediate the body pushes. The two table bases 0x016d6d30 and 0x016d6d70 live in the two 0xfbaf* CALLEES, not in this body, and are named only in the package header and in this sidecar -- both outside the reconstructed function's span.
mechanics.receiver_writes: exactly two: 0x00fa73f2 `ADD DWORD PTR [ESI+0x79c],EAX` and 0x00fa7442 `INC DWORD PTR [ESI+0x814]`. That is the machine-derived receiver record's written_through 2. The model test asserts it as a byte-level fact: a second call on the same fixture must leave all 0x818 receiver bytes plus a 16-byte sentinel tail unchanged outside those two four-byte windows.

return_semantics.value: no value is produced for the caller. The only outputs are the change to the word at receiver+0x79c, the increment of the word at receiver+0x814, the three dispatched calls' effects on the sub-object at receiver+0x28, and the two calls' effects on the sub-object at receiver+0x20c.
return_semantics.eax_residue: EAX is live at 0x00fa744b holding 0x00fbaf50's own return word. This is documented and deliberately NOT modelled, and the model test asserts nothing about it, because nothing in this body writes EAX for its caller after 0x00fa741e and 0x00fa7442 does not touch EAX. Whether any of this body's callers consumes that word is not established by any record in this repository.
return_semantics.ownership: the body performs no reference acquisition or release of its own. It reads two words and hands three addresses to callees. Whether the sub-objects at receiver+0x28 and +0x20c are owned, borrowed or smart handles is not established and is not claimed.

evidence.decompiler_disagreements: used as a hint and overruled by the listing in three places, each resolved in favour of the bytes. (1) Its arithmetic line `((iVar2 >> 5) - (iVar2 >> 0x1f)) * 0xac` computes a SIGNED shift right by 31 and then SUBTRACTS, which as written is not what 0x00fa73e7/0x00fa73ea do: the machine is `MOV EAX,EDX; SHR EAX,0x1f; ADD EAX,EDX`, a LOGICAL shift yielding 0 or 1, added not subtracted. Emulating the decompiler's line reproduces the wrong quotient for a negative delta.
